precepts.text: This is the Lord speaking to Cain: if thou doest well, shalt thou not be accepted? And if thou doest not well, sin lieth at the door. And now he switches: and unto thee, talking to Satan, shall be his desire, Cain's desire; and thou, Satan, shalt rule over him.
precepts.point: Even him, whose coming is after the working of Satan: our comings is supposed to be after Christ the Lord, but the white man's comings and goings is after Satan. That goes back to Genesis 4.

note.label: Drowning in Sin & Perdition

precepts.why:
Paul says the Wicked's “coming is after the working of Satan.” Our comings are supposed to be after Christ the Lord, but the white man's comings and goings are after Satan, and that goes back to Genesis 4.

The Lord speaks to Cain: “If thou doest well, shalt thou not be accepted? and if thou doest not well, sin lieth at the door.” Then the speech switches. “And unto thee shall be his desire”: now he is talking to Satan. Cain's desire shall be unto Satan, “and thou shalt rule over him”: Satan shall rule over Cain.

So from the beginning Cain was put under Satan's rule, and his line has walked after Satan ever since. That is why the coming of the man of sin is “after the working of Satan with all power and signs and lying wonders”: he is following the one who was set to rule over his father.

precepts.text: This is Cain's kids: unto Enoch was born Irad, and Mehujael begat Methusael, and Methusael begat Lamech. So Cain had a son named Enoch, one named Methusael, and one named Lamech. Two is always: the left hand side of wickedness and the righteous side. Cain had his Lamech and his Enoch; Seth's line had its Lamech and its Enoch. Righteous Enoch, evil Enoch.
precepts.point: And Noah was five hundred years old: and Noah begat Shem, Ham, and Japheth.

note.label: As in the Days of Noah: Past & Present

precepts.why:
These are Cain's children: “And unto Enoch was born Irad: and Irad begat Mehujael: and Mehujael begat Methusael: and Methusael begat Lamech.” So Cain had a son named Enoch, a descendant named Methusael, and one named Lamech.

Now set that beside Genesis 5, Seth's line: Jared begat Enoch, Enoch begat Methuselah, Methuselah begat Lamech, and Lamech begat Noah. The same names on both sides. It is always two: the left hand side of wickedness and the righteous side. Cain had his Lamech and his Enoch; Seth's line had its Lamech and its Enoch. Righteous Enoch, evil Enoch.

That is Ecclesiasticus 33 lived out in the generations before the flood: “there are two and two, one against another.” And the righteous line, the one named in Genesis 5, is the line of prophets that led to Noah, “a just man and perfect in his generations.”

precepts.text: Jubal was the father of all such as handle the harp: Cain's line handled music. They are behind all the music back then. Music is very influential, very powerful if it's in the wrong hands. Is it in the wrong hands today? Yes, it is. And Tubalcain, an instructor of every artificer in brass and iron, which would be what? Weapons. So Cain had power over entertainment, and power over weaponry, warfare. Remember Esau was a man of war; that was Esau's blessing. That was Cain's blessing too. Nothing new under the sun.
precepts.point: Not Noah. Noah didn't. And again, in process of time, thou broughtest the flood upon those that dwelt in the world, and destroyedst them. Nevertheless one of them thou leftest, namely Noah with his household, of whom came all righteous men: that goes back to Shem's line. Not Ham's line, not Japheth's line: Shem's line.

note.label: As in the Days of Noah: Past & Present

precepts.why:
Ezra says that after Adam transgressed, death came “in him and in his generations, of whom came nations, tribes, people, and kindreds, out of number.” Genesis 4 shows one of those lines: Cain's. And in Cain's line, “Jubal: he was the father of all such as handle the harp and organ.”

Cain's line handled the music. They were behind all the music back then, and music is very influential, very powerful when it is in the wrong hands. Is it in the wrong hands today? Yes, it is.

Then Tubal-cain was “an instructer of every artificer in brass and iron”, and brass and iron mean weapons. So Cain had power over entertainment and power over weaponry and warfare. Remember Esau was a man of war; that was Esau's blessing, and it was Cain's blessing too. There is nothing new under the sun.

This is how “every people walked after their own will, and did wonderful things before thee, and despised thy commandments.” Wonderful there means evil; they started to mess around with the daughters of men. And they despised the commandments, which shows the commandments were around back then; that is how Noah knew clean from unclean. The wicked had the music and the weapons then, the same as they do now, and it ended in the flood that destroyed them.

precepts.text: Seth was Abel's replacement of righteousness. Then began men to call upon the name of the Lord: when the sons of God despised God's commandments, God stopped dealing with us. But once Seth had Enos, that line began to call upon the name of the Lord, and God started dealing with us again. The wickedness is always around, and the righteous is born within the evil, always.
precepts.point: Not Noah. Noah didn't. And again, in process of time, thou broughtest the flood upon those that dwelt in the world, and destroyedst them. Nevertheless one of them thou leftest, namely Noah with his household, of whom came all righteous men: that goes back to Shem's line. Not Ham's line, not Japheth's line: Shem's line.

note.label: As in the Days of Noah: Past & Present

precepts.why:
After Cain slew Abel, “Adam knew his wife again; and she bare a son, and called his name Seth: For God, said she, hath appointed me another seed instead of Abel.” Seth was Abel's replacement, the replacement of righteousness in the earth.

“And to Seth, to him also there was born a son; and he called his name Enos: then began men to call upon the name of the Lord.” Ezra says the nations that came out of Adam “despised thy commandments.” When the sons of God despised God's commandments, God stopped dealing with us. But once Seth had Enos, that line began to call upon the name of the Lord, and God started dealing with us again.

Those tribes back then were called the sons of God. Tribes, sons of God: that sounds like the Israelites. Nothing new under the sun. The tribes of the sons of God were around back then and they are around now; wicked, evil leaders were around back then, and the righteous are around now. The wickedness is always around, and the righteous are always born within the evil.

That line carries straight to the flood. Ezra says God brought the flood on those that dwelt in the world, “Nevertheless one of them thou leftest, namely, Noah with his household, of whom came all righteous men.” That goes back to Shem's line: not Ham's line, not Japheth's line, but Shem's, the line that came down from Seth.

precepts.text: But when the unrighteous went away from her in his anger, he perished also in the fury wherewith he murdered his brother. Cain murdered Abel, and Cain was killed the same way. The judgment catches up.
precepts.point: The fugitive and vagabond speaks of his descendants. Has America paid for its crimes? Have the whites in South Africa paid? In Australia? None of them has paid for their crimes yet.

note.label: Job Sees America's 250th Anniversary

precepts.why:
Cain said, “Behold, thou hast driven me out this day from the face of the earth; and from thy face shall I be hid”: God was not dealing with him anymore. “and I shall be a fugitive and a vagabond in the earth.” A fugitive is somebody always on the run, someone who never pays for his crimes. A vagabond is in everybody's land and everybody's home.

But Cain did not escape forever. Wisdom shows he was put to death: “But when the unrighteous went away from her in his anger, he perished also in the fury wherewith he murdered his brother.” Cain murdered Abel, and Cain was killed the same way. The judgment caught up with him.

So what did it mean, I shall be a fugitive and a vagabond? It speaks of his descendants. Has America paid for its crimes? Have the whites in South Africa paid? In Australia? None of them has paid for their crimes yet. They have been on the run from justice, living in everybody's land.

That goes with Job 20, read in the same class: “His bones are full of the sin of his youth.” The fugitive has never paid, but as Cain perished in the fury wherewith he murdered his brother, judgment will come on his children. As Job said, “he shall vomit them up again”: everything taken will be restored.

precepts.point: That is why we read in Ecclesiasticus, never trust thine enemy. You think he forgot how we handled them under King David, or the dark ages? He has not forgotten; he is still acting out his vengeance on the so called blacks and Hispanics to this day.

note.label: 70 Times 7: The Perfection of Mercy Through Christ

precepts.why:
God said of Cain, “whosoever slayeth Cain, vengeance shall be taken on him sevenfold.” Then Cain’s great-great-grandson Lamech boasted to his wives, Adah and Zillah: “I have slain a man to my wounding, and a young man to my hurt. If Cain shall be avenged sevenfold, truly Lamech seventy and sevenfold.” He walked in the same footsteps as Cain; through regeneration it would be no surprise if Lamech were Cain all over again. Seventy and sevenfold in the mouth of a murderer means complete vengeance: total and utter.

That is why Ecclesiasticus says never trust thine enemy. You think he forgot how we handled him under King David, when we put garrisons over him and pushed him off the mountains? Or that we pushed him into the wilderness, where they became the wildlings of the dark ages? He has not forgotten. He is still acting out his vengeance on the so-called blacks and Hispanics to this day.

Ezekiel 35:5 names it: “Because thou hast had a perpetual hatred, and hast shed the blood of the children of Israel by the force of the sword in the time of their calamity, in the time that their iniquity had an end.” Perpetual hatred is great hatred, ongoing hatred, fiery hatred. That is Lamech’s seventy and sevenfold carried on through Edom.

The death of Patrice Lumumba shows it. One of the officers responsible spoke on video, laughing, this damn devil: they chopped up his body and poured acid on it, and he kept Lumumba’s gold tooth. His family held it until it was recently flown back to the Congo. The same was done to Nat Turner, whose skull was passed down as an heirloom, a trophy. These people are the damn devil the Bible speaks of, and that is the perpetual hatred.

precepts.text: For three transgressions of Edom, and for four, I will not turn away the punishment thereof; because he did pursue his brother with the sword, and did cast off all pity, and his anger did tear perpetually, and he kept his wrath for ever.
precepts.point: That is why we read in Ecclesiasticus, never trust thine enemy. You think he forgot how we handled them under King David, or the dark ages? He has not forgotten; he is still acting out his vengeance on the so called blacks and Hispanics to this day.

precepts.why:
Lamech’s “seventy and sevenfold” was complete vengeance, and Edom carries that same spirit. Amos 1:11: “Thus saith the Lord; For three transgressions of Edom, and for four, I will not turn away the punishment thereof; because he did pursue his brother with the sword, and did cast off all pity, and his anger did tear perpetually, and he kept his wrath for ever.”

He pursued his brother Jacob with the sword. He cast off all pity. His anger tore perpetually, and “he kept his wrath for ever.” Forever, perpetual: he hates our guts, and it does not wear off with time.

That is why we cannot trust this man, and why people wonder to this day why they still treat us the way they do. He has not forgotten how we ruled over him, and he is still acting out his vengeance. The Lord has seen it, and he says he will not turn away the punishment for it.

This is the dark side of seventy times seven. On the one side is the murderer’s total vengeance, kept forever; on the other side, as the class went on to show, is Christ answering Peter, “I say not unto thee, Until seven times: but, Until seventy times seven”: complete, boundless mercy for Israel.

precepts.why:
Edom’s hatred is perpetual, like Lamech’s vengeance, “seventy and sevenfold,” complete and total. But God has spoken on what will come of it. Obadiah 1:10: “For thy violence against thy brother Jacob shame shall cover thee, and thou shalt be cut off for ever.”

For his violence against his brother Jacob, shame shall cover him, and he shall be cut off forever. His wrath is kept forever, and his end is forever too.

So Lamech’s seventy and seven was complete vengeance, driven by hatred, perpetual hatred. Then comes the flip side. Peter asked, “Lord, how oft shall my brother sin against me, and I forgive him? till seven times?” and “Jesus saith unto him, I say not unto thee, Until seven times: but, Until seventy times seven.” Christ took the same number and made it complete mercy. He forgave us through all our captivities, and he commands us to forgive our brother the same way, while the enemy who kept his wrath for ever is cut off for ever.

note.label: Bitterness: The Hidden Leaven From Cain To Esau

precepts.why:
Cain was born first, just like Esau. “Abel was a keeper of sheep, but Cain was a tiller of the ground”, a man of the field, which already tells you what is going on. “And in process of time it came to pass, that Cain brought of the fruit of the ground an offering unto the Lord.” Cain already knew right from wrong, because his father taught him animal sacrifice, but over a process of time Cain turned evil and did not do what the Lord commanded.

Abel brought “of the firstlings of his flock and of the fat thereof. And the Lord had respect unto Abel and to his offering:” “But unto Cain and to his offering he had not respect. And Cain was very wroth, and his countenance fell.” His countenance fell because he was corrected. What really started all of this? Correction.

Solomon says, “Correction is grievous unto him that forsaketh the way”. Cain had forsaken the way over a process of time, so the correction was grievous to him. That grievous spirit nourished bitterness, and the bitterness grew until he murdered his brother. That is the spirit you are rolling in when you move with a bitter spirit.

Then: “and he that hateth reproof shall die”, because the wages of sin is death. Paul says, “For if we would judge ourselves, we should not be judged.” If we judged ourselves we would not have to be told about the bitterness, envy, hatred and malice inside us; when we refuse, the Lord has to bring the chastening. Cain refused to get himself right, and he became the father of wickedness.

Bitterness does not travel alone. Envy, pride, hatred and evil suspicion come bundled together like a cable TV package. Solomon names one: “Only by pride cometh contention”.

Cain was contending because pride was on him. Cain's attitude was: I am not going to make it right with my brother; my brother is the one who is off; in fact, I have to put him to death, because he is making me look bad. That is pride. Cain did not want to take the correction.

Then: “but with the well advised is wisdom.” The well advised are the ones who do well, like Abel. Wisdom says, let me get my spirit right; I cannot have an evil eye toward my brother. When correction comes, pride contends with it, while wisdom takes it and makes things right with the brother.

Then comes confusion. All of a sudden Cain did not know right from wrong, and every evil work followed: he slew his brother. When you are confused, saying, I do not know where this is coming from, every evil work will be the result.

Confusion is Satan's playground. Satan loves us operating in confusion. That is why his children throw every kind of confusion into the media and everywhere they go, and why leaders of other nations have said they do not want that American media in their countries. They know every evil work hides behind that cloud of confusion.

“Let us not be desirous of vain glory, provoking one another, envying one another.” Cain wanted to be the man; that is vain glory.

Provoking one another means agitating a brother to play him out of position, because you are envious of him. You do something to provoke him to evil so you can justify your position against him.

We see this even in marriage. A brother provokes his wife, she leaves the house and does something foolish, and he sits back saying, I told you the sister was off, I told you she was evil. No, brother: you are the evil one, you provoked your wife. We are not going for that foolishness here. Envy provokes, and provoking is how the bitter spirit sets up its victim.

The law says thou shalt not hate thy brother in thine heart; when you meditate on it you realize, I have the evil spirit toward the brother. The law is the light, like fog lights piercing through the cloud of confusion, and what you see on the other side is yourself in the mirror of the Bible.

precepts.why:
What is bitterness? It is sin. “For sin, taking occasion by the commandment, deceived me, and by it slew me.” Taking occasion by the commandment means you can only recognize sin through the commandments of God. How do you know you are in the middle of sin? The law says you shall not hate your brother in your heart, and when you meditate on it you realize, I have an evil spirit toward that brother. The law brings it to the surface.

Sin “deceived me”: you did not know bitterness was a sin, because you were deceived. But the law gives clarity. Like fog lights, it pierces the cloud of confusion. That is why the law is called a light: so you can see through the nonsense your mind was thinking.

Then sin “by it slew me.” When the scripture comes out, you feel cut, because you are no longer deceived and can see clearly. What you see on the other side of the fog is yourself in the mirror of the Bible, realizing how evil you were. Some people do not like the light and love to walk in darkness, saying, do not call that out, that is not me; brothers wearing purple and gold, a ribbon of blue and fringes, who are only blue ribbon Christians. We do not want to be those night walkers.

precepts.why:
“Cease from anger, and forsake wrath: fret not thyself in any wise to do evil.” That bitterness is the spirit of Cain, and in that wrath you might slay a brother, or in that bitterness you might betray one. None of us is above this. Do not sit in the congregation thinking so-and-so is getting cut with the scriptures; brother, that is you. Every lesson the leadership brings out is for us. The moment you think, I am not dealing with that, Satan already has you lined up and counts you on his team.

Go back to Genesis 4:8: “And Cain talked with Abel his brother”. This is the deception. Cain acted like his friend, talking with him over time about his flocks, until he could lure him out to the field: “when they were in the field, that Cain rose up against Abel his brother, and slew him.” Solomon describes that man: “He that hateth dissembleth with his lips, and layeth up deceit within him;” “When he speaketh fair, believe him not: for there are seven abominations in his heart.” Murder, envy, pride and covetousness are all in there. “Whose hatred is covered by deceit, his wickedness shall be shewed before the whole congregation.” That is why it is called a root of bitterness: roots are covered by soil where nobody can see them, but the Lord always brings it to the surface. “Whoso diggeth a pit shall fall therein”, and “a flattering mouth worketh ruin.”

John names the spirit: “Not as Cain, who was of that wicked one, and slew his brother.” Cain was the first recorded hater in the scriptures, and he came back as Esau. The scribes and Pharisees were bitter toward Christ and wanted him dead; carry an evil eye toward your brother and you are in the same spirit. “We know that we have passed from death unto life, because we love the brethren. He that loveth not his brother abideth in death.” “Whosoever hateth his brother is a murderer”. And Sirach warns, “When the ungodly curseth Satan, he curseth his own soul.” Brothers say, the white man is the devil, they are going to be destroyed, they are going into captivity, and then carry hatred toward their own brother, moving in the same spirit.

“Be not hasty in thy spirit to be angry: for anger resteth in the bosom of fools.” Bitterness is a progression: it starts with a correction or an offense, then pride comes in and you will not speak to the brother, then when you do speak it is in deceit, masking envy, anger and hatred, and in the end it destroys you and those around you. “A little leaven leaveneth the whole lump”: a little bitterness defiles the whole soul. Christ said, “Beware ye of the leaven of the Pharisees, which is hypocrisy.” “For there is nothing covered, that shall not be revealed”. Leaven looks flat at first and grows as it bakes, so do not let the hate bake. Deal with your brother and sister uprightly according to the laws of God before it festers and overcomes you.

precepts.why:
“Unto Adam also and to his wife did the Lord God make coats of skins, and clothed them.” That don't mean they were butt naked and needed clothes. It means God gave them a way to get forgiveness of their sin. Animal sacrifice was introduced right here, in Genesis 3:21: God clothed them with righteousness and forgiveness.

That is the key to Genesis 4. Cain “brought of the fruit of the ground an offering unto the Lord.” Abel “brought of the firstlings of his flock and of the fat thereof.” “And the Lord had respect unto Abel and to his offering”, because Abel's offering was in accordance with Genesis 3:21. Cain did not roll that way. He decided he was not going to do what God said and brought fruits and vegetables instead.

“But unto Cain and to his offering he had not respect. And Cain was very wroth, and his countenance fell.” His countenance falling means he got mad. He got pissed off. God asked him, “Why art thou wroth? and why is thy countenance fallen?” and told him, “If thou doest well, shalt thou not be accepted? and if thou doest not well, sin lieth at the door.” Doing well was obeying what God had set in place; sin lying at the door was disobedience.

So the difference between Cain and Abel was not the gift; it was obedience. Abel followed the way God had already shown his parents, and Cain replaced it with his own way. That disobedience is where Cain's line started.

precepts.text: Thy desire shall be to thy husband: if she desires anything, whether it is wisdom, knowledge, or money, it must be to her husband. That is the pattern for understanding Genesis 4:7.
precepts.point: If Cain shall be avenged sevenfold, truly Lamech seventy and sevenfold. They did not just kill the one man that hurt Lamech; they wiped out that whole lineage. That is how Esau gets down; remember who their desire was to.

note.label: Religion - The False Prophet

precepts.why:
God said to Cain, “And unto thee shall be his desire, and thou shalt rule over him.” This is a parable. God is speaking about the spiritual demon, Satan: the “thee” is Satan, and it is Cain's desire that would be unto him.

To see the pattern, go back to Genesis 3:16. “Unto the woman he said, I will greatly multiply thy sorrow and thy conception; in sorrow thou shalt bring forth children; and thy desire shall be to thy husband, and he shall rule over thee.” If a woman desires anything, whether it is sex, wisdom, knowledge or money, it must be to her husband, and he rules over her.

Read Genesis 4:7 with that in mind. Just as a woman's desire is to her husband, Cain's desire would be to Satan. Anything Cain wanted, he would have to go to Satan for it, and Satan would rule over him.

So Satan was over Cain and over his seed. When we read about Cain's children, the city, the cattle, the music, the weapons and Lamech's vengeance, we should not read them as holy and righteous. This is Cain's seed, and their desire is always unto Satan.

precepts.text: For the good are good things created from the beginning: from the time of Cain and Abel. The principal things for the whole use of man's life are water, fire, iron, salt, flour of wheat, honey, milk, the blood of the grape, oil, and clothing. All these things are for good to the godly: so to the sinners they are turned into evil. Think about today: what do they do with food? GMOs; they put things inside the chicken and the cows to make them larger, and it causes sickness. They monopolize water and bottle it. With fire they create bombs, even nuclear fire. With iron they make bullets and guns to kill people. The milk today is not the same milk we drank as children. Mixed fabrics in the clothing. Everything good, the sinful man turns to evil.

note.label: Religion - The False Prophet

precepts.why:
After Abel was slain, “Cain knew his wife; and she conceived, and bare Enoch: and he builded a city”. If Cain was the only child left, why would he need to build a city? There were already thousands upon thousands of people on the earth. He named the city after his son Enoch, and down the line came Lamech, who took two wives, the first time multiple wives appear in scripture.

Adah bore Jabal, “the father of such as dwell in tents, and of such as have cattle.” What could be wrong with tents and cattle? Ecclesiasticus answers: “For the good are good things created from the beginning: so evil things for sinners.” From the beginning means from the time of Cain and Abel. “The principal things for the whole use of man’s life are water, fire, iron, and salt, flour of wheat, honey, milk, and the blood of the grape, and oil, and clothing.” “All these things are for good to the godly: so to the sinners they are turned into evil.”

Bring it up to today. What do they do with food? GMOs, and things put inside the chicken and the cows to make them larger, and that causes sickness. They monopolize water and bottle it. With fire they create bombs, even nuclear fire. With iron they make bullets and guns to kill people. The milk today is not the same milk we drank as children. The clothing is made of mixed fabrics. Everything good, the sinful man turns to evil.

That is Cain's city. Jabal dealt in cattle with pricing and unrighteousness. His brother Jubal was “the father of all such as handle the harp and organ”, and it was not holy music: it was music about shake your ass, show me what you going with. Damn. It was songs about murder, drugs, debauchery and adultery, the same wicked songs many love today. Zillah bore Tubal-cain, “an instructer of every artificer in brass and iron”: that man was making all kinds of weapons. Good things created from the beginning, turned into evil by the seed whose desire was to Satan.

note.label: Religion - The False Prophet

precepts.why:
“As a nail sticketh fast between the joinings of the stones; so doth sin stick close between buying and selling.” When you are dealing in business with a sinner, the balances will be offset, because he always takes the favor, exceedingly. He will not take a five percent interest; he wants a hundred or two hundred percent.

That opens up Jabal, “the father of such as dwell in tents, and of such as have cattle.” It sounds harmless, but this is the seed of Cain in Cain's city. Jabal was dealing in tents and cattle with pricing and unrighteousness, buying and selling with sin stuck fast in between.

What Cain's seed did in the city of Enoch is what sinners do in business today. There is no new thing under the sun.

precepts.text: In this the children of God are manifest, and the children of the devil. John was telling the Israelites he wrote to: love one another, not as Cain, who was of that wicked one. Cain was under Satan; Satan was his father. And wherefore slew he him? Because his own works were evil, and his brother's righteous.
precepts.point: If Cain shall be avenged sevenfold, truly Lamech seventy and sevenfold. They did not just kill the one man that hurt Lamech; they wiped out that whole lineage. That is how Esau gets down; remember who their desire was to.

note.label: Religion - The False Prophet

precepts.why:
In case anyone doubts that Satan ruled over Cain, John explains it: “In this the children of God are manifest, and the children of the devil: whosoever doeth not righteousness is not of God, neither he that loveth not his brother.” There are children of God on the earth, and there are children of the devil.

John was correcting the Israelites he wrote to: “For this is the message that ye heard from the beginning, that we should love one another.” “Not as Cain, who was of that wicked one, and slew his brother.” He was telling them, do not be like Cain. And who is that wicked one? The devil of verse 10. Cain was under Satan; Satan was his father.

“And wherefore slew he him? Because his own works were evil, and his brother’s righteous.” That is Genesis 4: Abel did well and was accepted, Cain did not do well, his desire went to Satan, and “Cain rose up against Abel his brother, and slew him.”

It shows in Cain's seed. Lamech said, “I have slain a man to my wounding, and a young man to my hurt.” “If Cain shall be avenged sevenfold, truly Lamech seventy and sevenfold.” They did not just kill the one man who hurt Lamech; they wiped out that whole lineage: the sons, the daughters, the aunts, the grandparents. That is how Esau gets down too. Remember who their desire was to: Satan. Everybody comes from Adam, but not everybody is a child of God.

precepts.text: If thou doest well, shalt thou not be accepted? and if thou doest not well, sin lieth at the door. Doing well is a covenant with God's commandments: I will not watch, eat, touch, or taste that. Doing not well is a covenant with death, Satan's commandments; every disagreement with God's commandment is an agreement with Satan's. Agree to go past the alcohol limit and you let a spirit take your body; agree with the thought that you do not like that sister and you spread gossip through the body; agree with the hunger pains and the smell and a gluttony spirit is on you. A contract with the thought lets the demon tunnel through the five senses to full possession.
precepts.point: There are spirits in an unseen realm communicating through your mind, telling you what to think. You cannot stop the thoughts, but whether you take hold of them is your decision: agree and act, or disagree and go another way.

note.label: Power Under Control: Food, Sex & Self-Mastery

precepts.why:
God told Cain, “If thou doest well, shalt thou not be accepted? and if thou doest not well, sin lieth at the door.” Demons do not simply possess someone; it is a process, and they need a series of yeses. The spirits can only communicate through your thoughts and set the stage. To take full control, you have to agree with the thought, make a contract or covenant with it, and act on it. If you say, I do not agree with that, that is not according to the scriptures, the demon cannot take control of your eyes, your ears, your mouth or your tongue.

Doing well is keeping the commandments. It is a covenant with God: I am not going to watch that, eat that, touch that, taste that. Doing not well, sin lying at the door, is a covenant with death, a covenant with Satan. Satan has commandments too, and any time you disagree with keeping God's commandment, you agree to keep Satan's.

See how the yeses add up. You agree to go past the blood alcohol limit and you let a spirit take control of your body, then wonder why you slept with that person. A thought says, I do not like that sister, you agree with it and start gossiping, and now it spreads through the whole body. You know that food is not for you, but you agree with the hunger pains, the sight of it and the smell of it, and now a gluttony spirit is on you. Every contract with a thought lets the demon tunnel through the five senses to full possession of your vessel.

The answer is in Galatians 5:16: “Walk in the Spirit, and ye shall not fulfil the lust of the flesh.” Walk in the spirit by studying, keeping a strong unit, sitting at the doorsteps of the Bishop and the Deacons, and addicting yourself to God's word, and you will not have time to entertain the flesh. Stop feeding your mind hours of shows and music that taint your thinking. Reprogram and rewire yourself to develop godly habits, because “the flesh lusteth against the Spirit, and the Spirit against the flesh”.

Christ is the example. His disciples prayed him, “Master, eat”, and he said, “I have meat to eat that ye know not of.” He was the master of his own vessel: his sight, smell, taste, hearing and thoughts. Nobody programmed him but the Father. “My meat is to do the will of him that sent me, and to finish his work.” That should be our agenda: to consume the scriptures, to see, taste, hear and believe them. That is our meat and our life.

precepts.text: Not as Cain, who was of that wicked one, and slew his brother, because his own works were evil and his brother's righteous. Cain was the seed of the devil.
precepts.point: Cain rose up and slew Abel. That is the fulfilment of Genesis 3:15 and the first blood shed in the war: Cain, Satan's seed, killed our forefather.

note.label: Fighting Satan - the War Within

precepts.why:
Genesis 4 shows Satan’s children being born in the earth. Eve bare Cain and then Abel; Abel kept sheep and Cain tilled the ground. “And the Lord had respect unto Abel and to his offering: But unto Cain and to his offering he had not respect. And Cain was very wroth”. The Lord told him, “If thou doest well, shalt thou not be accepted? and if thou doest not well, sin lieth at the door. And unto thee shall be his desire, and thou shalt rule over him.” Do good and you will be accepted; do evil and Satan will rule over you. Cain would become the child of Satan and serve him.

Then Cain talked with Abel, “and it came to pass, when they were in the field, that Cain rose up against Abel his brother, and slew him”. That is the fulfillment of Genesis 3:15, “I will put enmity between thee and the woman, and between thy seed and her seed”. The enmity started there. Cain, Satan’s seed, killed our forefather: the first murder on the earth and the first blood shed in the war.

John proves Cain was that seed: “Not as Cain, who was of that wicked one, and slew his brother. And wherefore slew he him? Because his own works were evil, and his brother’s righteous.” Cain was always evil. His descendants were the children of the devil, and they corrupted everyone on the earth, even the sons of God, until God destroyed the world. All the evil you see Esau doing on the earth today, Cain was doing back then.

Then the sons of God and the sons of the devil came back. Rebekah’s children “struggled together within her”, and the Lord said, “Two nations are in thy womb, and two manner of people shall be separated from thy bowels”. Jacob is the twelve tribes, the so-called Negroes and Hispanics; Esau is the so-called white man. This fight did not start with slavery, Jim Crow or civil rights; it started in the beginning with Cain and Abel, and was reborn as Jacob and Esau: good against evil. Many of our people followed Cain then, and many follow Esau now and have become children of the devil themselves.

Esau “came out red, all over like an hairy garment”, born without pigment, as Cain lost his when the earth cursed him. Jacob took hold on his heel, a prophetic sign of Genesis 3:15: our Lord coming to destroy Satan and his children. And when scripture says “the devil shall cast some of you into prison”, it was Herod, an Edomite, who “killed James the brother of John with the sword” and took Peter. The devil means the deceiver, and it is interchangeable: the father and his children, who can do nothing without the father that dwells in them.

precepts.text: If thou doest not well, sin lieth at the door, and unto thee shall be his desire, and thou shalt rule over him. Satan became Cain's father.
precepts.point: Cain's line died in the flood, but all spirits return. Cain came back as Esau and Abel, or Seth, came back as Jacob.

note.label: Edom's Achilles' Heel

precepts.why:
In the garden, before Adam and Eve were put out, God said, “I will put enmity between thee and the woman, and between thy seed and her seed”. Enmity is hatred. Satan has seed on this earth, and the woman’s seed, the descendants who would come through her, is Israel. When that was spoken, Cain was not yet born. The seed of Satan was Cain.

Genesis 4 shows how. “And the Lord said unto Cain, Why art thou wroth? and why is thy countenance fallen? If thou doest well, shalt thou not be accepted?” If you obey me, will you not be accepted by me? But “and if thou doest not well”, if you choose to break my commandments, “sin lieth at the door. And unto thee shall be his desire, and thou shalt rule over him.” The one spoken of there is Satan: Satan would be Cain’s desire, and would rule over him. Satan would be Cain’s god and Cain’s father.

Cain chose not to obey, and he killed Abel. From that moment the enmity of Genesis 3:15 was at work in the earth: the seed of the serpent against the seed of the woman.

It did not end with Cain. His line died in the flood, but all spirits return. Cain came back as Esau, the one who “came out red, all over like an hairy garment”, and Abel, or Seth, came back as Jacob, whose hand took hold on Esau’s heel. So Genesis 3:15 and Genesis 4:7 explain the hatred Edom has for Israel to this day: it is the enmity God put between the two seeds in the beginning.

precepts.text: Jacob have I loved, but Esau have I hated.
precepts.point: Cain was wroth and his countenance fell. The same reason Cain hated Abel is the reason Esau hates Jacob.

note.label: Raising Cain: The Son of Perdition, Merchants, and Captive Nations

precepts.why:
Cain “brought of the fruit of the ground an offering unto the Lord”, and Abel brought “of the firstlings of his flock and of the fat thereof.” “And the Lord had respect unto Abel and to his offering: But unto Cain and to his offering he had not respect.” What happened to Cain and Abel physically is a foreshadowing of Jacob and Esau spiritually: one is chosen and one is not.

Paul explains it with Rebecca’s twins: “For the children being not yet born, neither having done any good or evil, that the purpose of God according to election might stand, not of works, but of him that calleth”. Then: “As it is written, Jacob have I loved, but Esau have I hated.” Cain was not rejected because he was wroth; that was ordained from the beginning. It is about election, the purpose God makes. He can make one vessel for one use and another vessel of wrath fitted for destruction.

Christians take “not of works” to mean the law need not be kept. What it tells us is that from the foundation God chose his elect. He still requires the works of the law, not the sacrificial law, but being clean and repented, to obtain the kingdom of heaven. When the first world was formed every nation was supposed to follow the laws, and judgment followed whoever did not. Cain’s rebellious nature showed itself, and it continues to this day in Esau.

People say God doesn’t hate, and they isolate “God is love.” But notice it says “as it is written”: it is in the Bible. It was written first in Malachi: “Was not Esau Jacob’s brother? saith the Lord: yet I loved Jacob, And I hated Esau, and laid his mountains and his heritage waste for the dragons of the wilderness.” Edom says, “We are impoverished, but we will return and build the desolate places”, and he did, in the Renaissance. But the Lord says, “They shall build, but I will throw down; and they shall call them, The border of wickedness, and, The people against whom the Lord hath indignation for ever.” God lets him rise to power so that he can take him down.

And the Lord asked Cain, “Why art thou wroth? and why is thy countenance fallen?” Remember that, because the same reason Cain hated Abel is the reason Esau hates Jacob today. It is the same spirit; only the name changes. “Satan” simply means adversary, one who obstructs and opposes. That is why everything they do is about us: they were made for that purpose, to obstruct and oppose us, because God purposed it from the beginning.

precepts.text: If I sin, then thou markest me.
precepts.point: The Lord set a mark on Cain lest any should kill him. The mark is sin, which preserves the wicked until their judgment.

note.label: Raising Cain: The Son of Perdition, Merchants, and Captive Nations

precepts.why:
The Lord asked Cain, “Where is Abel thy brother?”, and he answered, “I know not: Am I my brother’s keeper?” But “the voice of thy brother’s blood crieth unto me from the ground. And now art thou cursed from the earth”. That curse is layered, but the ultimate curse is the utter destruction of Cain and his seed, and it has not yet been fulfilled. It is a deferred judgment, held “until the times of the Gentiles be fulfilled”: a set time that has to be fulfilled of these heathen nations, starting with Esau as the top one. It is the same spirit of Cain today. Unless we accept who this man is, the son of perdition, nothing else about the last days will make sense.

The Lord told him, “a fugitive and a vagabond shalt thou be in the earth”. Apart from the little land he had in the kingdom of Esau, he takes up the identity of others: he calls himself the Greeks, when the real Greeks were black, of the Japhetic seed; the Romans; the last samurai; the Israelites and the Egyptians in The Ten Commandments. The confusion of faces was supposed to be his curse, and he flipped it onto us, until we became the astonishment, the proverb and the byword.

Cain feared that “every one that findeth me shall slay me”, and “the Lord set a mark upon Cain, lest any finding him should kill him.” Why not judge him right then? Because God had a purpose for him, as he raised up Pharaoh so that his power would be magnified when he comes to redeem his people and the earth.

Job tells us what the mark is: “If I sin, then thou markest me, and thou wilt not acquit me from mine iniquity.” The mark is sin. And sin preserves him, because sin is witchcraft: by it he seduces the nations that might stand against him into the confederacy of Psalm 83. They all know what he is, but lust, the love of money and power, make them put that aside and ally with him, the way criminals make alliances knowing one day someone will stab them in the back. Under Trump that confederacy is starting to crack.

So Cain is protected only for a time. The judgment was promised through Esau: “I hated Esau, and laid his mountains and his heritage waste”, and they shall call them “The border of wickedness, and, The people against whom the Lord hath indignation for ever.” That border of wickedness is the mark. “The earth is given into the hand of the wicked: he covereth the faces of the judges thereof; if not, where, and who is he?” If not Esau, the United States of America, who is he? And “evil shall hunt the violent man to overthrow him”: his demise will come the same way he ruled.

precepts.text: The bewitching of naughtiness doth obscure things that are honest.
precepts.point: The Lord set a mark on Cain lest any should kill him. The mark is sin, which preserves the wicked until their judgment.

note.label: Raising Cain: The Son of Perdition, Merchants, and Captive Nations

precepts.why:
Why would a mark of sin protect Cain? Solomon answers: “For the bewitching of naughtiness doth obscure things that are honest; and the wandering of concupiscence doth undermine the simple mind.” Sin is bewitching. It is seductive. It hides what is honest, so that, as the scripture says, if it were possible even the elect would be deceived.

That is how the mark works. Cain’s line would have rulership for a time, and he would rule the earth with darkness, with sin and with evil, and people would be enticed by it, Israelites included. Our northern kingdom, the majority of it, fell for it, and now they are getting their wake-up call, though there was always a remnant that rebelled against the colonialism they saw in Latin America.

The bewitching is also how the confederacy holds together. The other nations know what he stands for; it is common knowledge. But the love of money, power and rulership says, put that aside, this is the one it was given to, nobody else could get me these things. So they ally with him, and there is no honor among thieves with this man. We watch him boast of taking Venezuela’s president in an operation so fast and violent, threaten the vice president with worse, and name Colombia and Mexico next.

But the spell does not last. “The pride of thine heart hath deceived thee, thou that dwellest in the clefts of the rock, whose habitation is high; that saith in his heart, Who shall bring me down to the ground?” We know who brings him down: first those he dealt with turn against him, and then Christ and his elect have the glory and honor of taking him down. The wicked are revealed and restrained for a time, a hedge around them until they fulfill what the Lord wants, and then comes their final judgment.

precepts.text: By thy sword shalt thou live.
precepts.point: Esau's blessing is by thy sword shalt thou live; he takes the fatness of the earth by violence.

note.label: Raising Cain: The Son of Perdition, Merchants, and Captive Nations

precepts.why:
Tubal-cain was “an instructer of every artificer in brass and iron”. He worked metal, and at that time metal meant tools of war; he was not making decorations for your house. The mark followed Cain’s lineage: sin, violence and hatred were in his spirit. Where an artist sees art in raw material, his mind saw weapons. Weaponry came into the earth, or at least advanced, through Cain’s line. Murder led to industry, hatred led to technology, and violence led to institutional power, the hegemony that controls everything.

Then that spirit comes through Esau. “Hast thou but one blessing, my father? bless me, even me also, O my father. And Esau lifted up his voice, and wept.” Isaac answered, “Behold, thy dwelling shall be the fatness of the earth, and of the dew of heaven from above”: he would have rulership and authority. And the connection to Tubal-cain: “And by thy sword shalt thou live”. The fatness of the earth, everything he has, he gets by violence.

Then: “and shalt serve thy brother; and it shall come to pass when thou shalt have the dominion, that thou shalt break his yoke from off thy neck”. That happened once our kingdom passed. We had a kingdom for a little while, and since then we have never been in any kind of power up to this day, while he increased through the process of time.

We see it in the graphic of Trump straddling the Western Hemisphere, the Monroe Doctrine renamed the Donroe Doctrine: this is mine. That is the one that sits upon many waters. The wicked are revealed, restrained for a time with a hedge around them to fulfill what the Lord wants, and then comes their final judgment.

precepts.text: I have created the smith that bringeth forth an instrument, and I have created the waster to destroy.
precepts.point: Esau's blessing is by thy sword shalt thou live; he takes the fatness of the earth by violence.

note.label: Raising Cain: The Son of Perdition, Merchants, and Captive Nations

precepts.why:
“Behold, I have created the smith that bloweth the coals in the fire, and that bringeth forth an instrument for his work”. The Lord is over all of it. He puts it on Satan, his emissary, and Satan passes it around. It is twofold: it speaks of the brass and iron of Tubal-cain, and then it names something more.

Notice “an instrument”: not all weaponry, one in particular. Then he names it: “and I have created the waster to destroy”. What weapon at that time could have been called the waster? Nothing. Zechariah describes it: “Their flesh shall consume away while they stand upon their feet, and their eyes shall consume away in their holes, and their tongue shall consume away in their mouth.” Nobody could have imagined such a weapon then. They had no word for nuclear weapons or atoms, so they saw visions and explained them the best they could: it is the waster.

Malachi says, “behold, the day cometh, that shall burn as an oven; and all the proud, yea, and all that do wickedly, shall be stubble”: Esau, the other nations, and rebellious Israel that does not repent. The day that cometh burns them so “it shall leave them neither root nor branch”. A fire leaves ash; this leaves nothing. Peter says “the elements shall melt with fervent heat”. The nations know it: their treaties against nuclear proliferation show the Lord staying their hand, because whoever uses one ends the world as they know it. Isaiah 29 says the strangers “shall be like small dust” and it shall be “at an instant suddenly”, not like regular fire, and all the nations that fight against Ariel, the lion of God, “even all that fight against her and her munition”, her weapons, “shall be as a dream of a night vision”, gone that quick. They filled their bellies and lived deliciously, and in an instant it is all gone. God put it in their spirit to make that thing, and he will use their own weapon, the thing that gave them their power and respect, to end them.

This should move us. The Lord “is longsuffering to us-ward”; the day waits until the set number is sealed, and it comes “as a thief in the night.” “Seeing then that all these things shall be dissolved, what manner of persons ought ye to be in all holy conversation and godliness”? Paul says the same: “let us watch and be sober”: do not drink of her wine, do not sleep thinking you are an American and nothing can touch you. “For God hath not appointed us to wrath, but to obtain salvation by our Lord Jesus Christ”. So “comfort yourselves together, and edify one another”: this is the time to be more united, not divided over simple issues. We look boldly for that day, because “we, according to his promise, look for new heavens and a new earth, wherein dwelleth righteousness”: a baptism by fire that cleanses the evil and makes the earth fit for the kingdom.

precepts.text: Esau hated Jacob and comforted himself, purposing to kill him.
precepts.point: Lamech boasted that he slew a young man to his hurt, and if Cain is avenged sevenfold, Lamech seventy and sevenfold. Murder became normal and celebrated.

note.label: Raising Cain: The Son of Perdition, Merchants, and Captive Nations

precepts.why:
Lamech told his wives, “I have slain a man to my wounding, and a young man to my hurt. If Cain shall be avenged sevenfold, truly Lamech seventy and sevenfold.” That was cold-blooded murder, killing with no anger behind it, for the thrill of it. Cain killed in anger; if he is judged, how much more Lamech, who just had violence in him. He boasted in it. It went beyond Cain; it increased. That is when murder was normalized and celebrated in that line.

That is why Esau has the same spirit: “And Esau hated Jacob because of the blessing wherewith his father blessed him: and Esau said in his heart, The days of mourning for my father are at hand; then will I slay my brother Jacob.” It is in his spirit till this day. Rebekah was told, “Behold, thy brother Esau, as touching thee, doth comfort himself, purposing to kill thee.” Killing is a comfort to him. Trump boasted that the Venezuela raid was very violent, and said of the boats, we are just going to kill them.

“Now therefore, my son, obey my voice; and arise, flee thou to Laban my brother to Haran”. The only thing Jacob could do was flee; he could not stand against that bloodthirsty violence. It is the same spirit as Cain: patient, vengeful and calculated. Cain lured his brother into the field; Esau said, I will wait until the days of mourning are done, and get him when he least suspects it.

That spirit is the son of perdition. “Let no man deceive you by any means: for that day shall not come, except there come a falling away first, and that man of sin be revealed, the son of perdition; Who opposeth and exalteth himself above all that is called God”.
